page_title: Code a Search Engine in PHP Part 1

sources.entry: PHP: _Code a Web Search Engine in PHP_

summary.title: Code a Search Engine in PHP Part 1
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build the crawler, inverted record-level index, document store and naive indexer of a small PHP search engine, using test-driven development.
keywords: build a search engine from scratch
takeaways: Seed a crawler from a URL list such as the Quantcast top million or DMOZ, and parse it with a short PHP or Python script.
Download pages in parallel with xargs -P and spread files across directories using an MD5 hash of the URL.
Design a record-level inverted index that stores 3 integers (doc id, count, pre-rank) per document in binary files, about 12 bytes per document.
Separate the index, document store, indexer, search and ranker behind interfaces so each can be unit tested and swapped later.
summary.summary: The author, writing in 2013, sets out to build a small search engine in PHP that can index about a million documents, and splits it into crawler, index, document store, indexer, search and ranker components defined by interfaces. The crawler section covers building a seed URL list from the Quantcast top million (and DMOZ as an alternative), then downloading pages with a simple file_get_contents loop parallelised via xargs and hashed into directories. The index section chooses a record-level inverted index stored as packed binary integers, with validation, store, get and clear methods, and estimates its size at about 6 GB for a million documents. The article ends with a naive indexer that builds word concordances and feeds the index and document store, and the code is shown inline throughout.
